newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia searching for more Timor brawl suspects.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia searching for more Timor brawl suspects.

text.p: Indonesian police said on Saturday they were searching for more suspects following brawls between young Catholics and members of a military-backed group earlier this month.

East Timor's deputy police chief, Lieutenant-Colonel Atok Rismanto, said the number of suspects in the incident in Viqueque might increase from the current 109. He denied a report that some of the youths had been released.

"We still question the 109 people. They could be charged with property destruction or carrying (a) sharp weapon, which is illegal here. We continue searching for more suspects," he told Reuters by telephone from Dili, the capital of East Timor.
He said Viqueque, about 100 km (60 miles) east of Dili, was calm.
A church source in Viqueque said on Saturday that 54 youths had been released and that there was no trouble overnight.
Church sources earlier said brawls erupted after members of the military-backed Gada Paksi youth organisation attacked 10 Catholic youths, a priest and his driver on February 7.

One source said the Gada Paksi members beat the priest and the youths because they accused them of trying to have an illegal meeting. Fights between the two groups continued until February 9, said the source.

The London-based rights group Amnesty International, in a statement on Saturday, urged Indonesian authorities to ensure that none of the detainees was tortured or ill-treated, and that were given immediate access to lawyers, family members or medical treatment when necessary.
Church sources said some of the detainees had been wounded during the brawls.

Gada Paksi, the Youth Guard of Integration Upholders, was set up in 1995 and its members receive military-style training in Java. East Timorese residents have accused members of the group of intimidating people who oppose the territory's integration with Indonesia.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later, a move not recognised by the United Nations.

The brawls were the latest incidents to rock East Timor. On December 24, a crowd welcoming Nobel Peace Prize winner Bishop Carlos Belo back to Dili attacked police and killed a local soldier in the grounds of the cathedral.
At least 15 people were arrested in connection with the Christmas Eve disturbances.
